title: Automate a Routine Report with Validation and Fallback
subtitle: Automate the data path, not hidden judgment.
description: Automate a stable reporting workflow only after defining source ownership, transformations, validation rules, freshness, failure handling, and a manual fallback.

lifeOsSource.hack: Automate a report only when the data path and failure behavior are explicit enough to validate.
lifeOsSource.whatYouDo: Map the report consumer, source data, transformations and delivery step. Define validation rules for schema, completeness, freshness and key totals. Build a small automated path with logging and a visible failure state, keep a manual fallback, and stop publication when validation fails.
lifeOsSource.checkIn: Did the automated report use the expected source, pass validation, arrive on time, and fail visibly when an assumption broke?

faq.question: What should happen when validation fails?
faq.answer: Fail visibly, preserve the last trustworthy state where appropriate, notify the owner, and use the manual fallback or repair path. Do not silently publish a result that no longer meets the contract.
faq.answerHtml: Fail visibly, preserve the last trustworthy state where appropriate, notify the owner, and use the manual fallback or repair path. Do not silently publish a result that no longer meets the contract.

intro.html: A report is not ready for automation merely because someone repeats it. Reliable automation needs an explicit data contract, validation, ownership, failure behavior, and a way to recover when an assumption changes.

sections.title: 1. Map the report contract
sections.html: Name the consumer, purpose, source systems, transformation logic, output, schedule, and owner. Mark manual judgments separately rather than hiding them inside code.

sections.title: 2. Define validation before automation
sections.html: Choose checks that would catch a wrong or stale report: expected schema, entity coverage, freshness, reconciled totals, duplicate rules, and important business constraints.

sections.title: 3. Build a visible failure and recovery path
sections.html: Log the run, surface validation failures, and stop or quarantine publication when the contract is broken. Assign an owner and preserve a manual recovery path.

editorialCuration.reason: Replace fabricated team savings, unsupported reliability targets, arbitrary engineering thresholds, and broad automation claims with a bounded report-automation readiness and control protocol.
